sql-001.base: What if you needed to find users who created duplicate accounts across different time periods?
variants: The same person signed up again a year after closing their first account. Should that count as a duplicate, and how would your query find it?
Marketing wants accounts created by the same email within 24 hours of each other. How do you change the query?

sql-001.base: How would you optimize this for a table with 100M rows?
variants: The users table grows by 2 million rows a day and the duplicate check runs hourly. How do you keep it fast?
Your duplicate query does a full table scan on 300M rows. What do you look at in the query plan, and what do you change?

sql-001.base: Should you use GROUP BY or DISTINCT? When would each fail?
variants: A colleague writes SELECT DISTINCT email FROM users to find duplicates. What does that return, and why doesn't it answer the question?
When would GROUP BY with HAVING give you something DISTINCT never can?

sql-002.base: How do you handle customers with zero historical payments or very new customers?
variants: A third of customers in a segment joined in the last 60 days. How do they enter your historical payment patterns?
Some customers have invoices but have never paid one yet. How do you represent them in the query output?

sql-002.base: Your query takes 15 minutes on 500M rows. How would you optimize it for daily runs?
variants: The query scans three years of payments every morning, but only yesterday's rows change. How do you restructure it?
The daily job joins 500M payments to a customer table on a computed segment column. Where is the time going, and what do you change?

sql-002.base: What do you do if payment behavior changed dramatically post-COVID? Do you use all history or recent-only?
variants: Payment terms changed for all customers in 2022. Do you keep the earlier history in the patterns, and how?
Customers paid much faster during a two-month promotion last year. How do you stop that period distorting the patterns?

sql-003.base: How would you identify customers at churn risk using this metric?
variants: A customer's longest gap is 200 days, but it was three years ago and they pay monthly now. Is longest gap the right churn signal?
How would you turn the gap metric into a list the collections team can act on each week?

sql-003.base: Your calculation includes refunds (negative payments). Should they reset the gap counter?
variants: Some payments are later reversed as chargebacks. Do they count when measuring the gap?
A customer pays one invoice in three installments on consecutive days. How should that affect the gap calculation?

sql-004.base: How do you handle customers who were active, churned, then came back?
variants: A customer is active in January, silent in February and back in March. Are they retained in March? How does your query decide?
How would you report retention so that customers who lapse and return are counted separately from those who never left?

sql-004.base: Your retention % for Jan cohort is higher than Dec. What could explain this (besides better product)?
variants: The March cohort retains much better than February's. What would you check before calling it a product win?
The January cohort is half the size of December's but retains better. What non-product explanations would you look for?

sql-005.base: Two people tie for third place. Do you return both, and how does that change your query?
variants: Three people share the second-highest salary in a department. With ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK, how many rows does each return?
HR says ties must all be included even if that returns five people. Which ranking function do you use, and why?

sql-005.base: A department has only two employees. What does your query return?
variants: A department has a single employee with a NULL salary. What does your query return for that department?
The business wants exactly three rows per department, even when it has fewer staff. Can SQL do that, and should it?

sql-005.base: Why can't you filter on the window function directly in the WHERE clause?
variants: Your query puts RANK() OVER (...) <= 3 in the WHERE clause and fails. Explain why, and show the fix.
Why does filtering on a window function need a subquery or CTE, but filtering on a regular column doesn't?

sql-006.base: Some days have no sales, so there is no row for them. What goes wrong?
variants: The store is closed every Sunday, so Sundays have no rows. What does ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW actually average over?
How would you make the rolling average treat missing days as zero revenue?

sql-006.base: What is the difference between ROWS and RANGE in the window frame?
variants: Two rows share the same date. How do ROWS and RANGE frames treat them differently?
Your database supports RANGE with an interval, like RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6 days' PRECEDING. What problem does that solve?

sql-006.base: What should the first six days of the series show?
variants: The dashboard shows a 7-day average for the first day of data. Is that misleading? What would you show instead?
How would you flag or filter rows where fewer than 7 days fed into the average?

sql-007.base: How would you handle events that arrive late or out of order?
variants: Mobile events can arrive up to two hours late. How do you handle sessions that are already computed when a late event lands?
Two events have the same timestamp to the millisecond. How does that affect your ordering and session boundaries?

sql-007.base: This table has 5 billion rows. How do you make it practical to run daily?
variants: Recomputing sessions over all history takes six hours. How do you process only new data each day without breaking sessions that cross midnight?
How would you partition the table so the daily sessionization job stays fast as data grows?

sql-007.base: How do bots or very long sessions affect your numbers?
variants: One user has a single session lasting 40 hours. What might be going on, and how do you handle it in your metrics?
Average session length jumped 30% overnight. What would you check before reporting it?

sql-008.base: Your NOT IN query suddenly returns zero rows. What could have happened?
variants: The February table has a few rows with a NULL customer_id. What happens to WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM feb)?
Why does NOT EXISTS behave differently from NOT IN when the subquery contains NULLs?

sql-008.base: NOT EXISTS, LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL, or NOT IN: how do you choose?
variants: The February table has 2 billion rows. Which of NOT EXISTS, LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL and NOT IN would you pick, and why?
A teammate finds NOT EXISTS hard to read and prefers LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL. Is there any difference in results?

sql-008.base: How would you generalize this to 'bought in at least 3 of the last 6 months but not this month'?
variants: How would you find customers who bought every month last quarter but not this month?
Extend the query to customers whose spend dropped by more than half from January to February.

sql-009.base: What should the query return if two people tie for the highest salary?
variants: Salaries are 100, 100 and 90. What should 'second highest' return, and which query gives that?
Your query uses LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 after ORDER BY salary DESC. What does it return when the top salary is shared?

sql-009.base: What if there is no second highest value at all?
variants: The table has one employee. What does your query return, and is that what the caller expects?
Should the query return NULL or no rows when there is no second highest salary? Why does it matter for the code calling it?

sql-009.base: How would you generalize this to the Nth highest salary per department?
variants: How would you find the third highest salary in each department, including departments with fewer than three salaries?
Write the query for the Nth highest salary where N is a parameter. Which ranking function do you use?

sql-010.base: When does a filter belong in WHERE and when in HAVING, if both would give the same result?
variants: You filter WHERE region = 'EU' and HAVING region = 'EU'. Both give the same result. Which is better, and why?
On a 1-billion-row table, what is the cost of putting a non-aggregate condition in HAVING instead of WHERE?

sql-010.base: What changes if you also want to exclude departments with fewer than 5 people?
variants: Now only include departments where the highest salary is under 200,000. Where does that condition go?
Return departments with an average salary above 50,000 and at least one employee hired this year. How do you write it?

sql-011.base: What should the first month for each product show?
variants: A product launched in March. What should its March growth figure be, and how does your query produce it?
Should the first month show NULL, 0% or be left out? Who reads this report, and how does that change your answer?

sql-011.base: What if a product has no sales in some months?
variants: A product sold nothing in May. Your LAG compares June with April. Why is that wrong, and how do you fix it?
How would you build a complete product-by-month grid before calculating growth?

sql-011.base: What if last month's revenue is zero?
variants: A product went from $0 to $5,000. What growth percentage do you report?
How do you stop a division by zero from failing the whole query?

sql-012.base: How would you find each user's longest streak ever?
variants: Return each user's current streak as of today. How does that differ from the longest streak?
How would you count how many separate 3-day streaks each user had this year?

sql-012.base: What if a user has several events on the same day?
variants: A user logs 50 events on one day. Why does your streak logic break if you don't handle that first?
Should a day with only a background ping count as active? How would you encode that in the query?

sql-012.base: What if 'day' depends on the user's time zone?
variants: Timestamps are stored in UTC, but users span 12 time zones. How do you assign events to days?
A user travels from New York to Tokyo mid-week. Whose calendar day defines their streak?

sql-013.base: How would you check for this before trusting a new join?
variants: Before shipping a new dashboard query with four joins, what quick checks do you run?
How do you confirm that a join key is unique on one side?

sql-013.base: Show a fix when you need both item-level and payment-level figures.
variants: Write the query so total revenue comes from order_items and total paid comes from payments, with no double counting.
Why does aggregating each table to the order level before joining fix the problem?

sql-013.base: Does the same problem appear with a LEFT JOIN?
variants: A colleague switches the payments join from INNER to LEFT to fix the doubling. Does that help?
Can the same doubling happen with a join on a dimension table? When?

sql-014.base: A column has 100 rows, 20 NULLs and 30 distinct non-null values. What do the three return?
variants: A column has 1,000 rows, all NULL. What do COUNT(*), COUNT(col) and COUNT(DISTINCT col) return?
A column has 50 rows: 10 NULL, and the rest are the values 'a' and 'b'. What do the three counts return?

sql-014.base: How do NULLs affect AVG and SUM?
variants: Salaries are 100, 200 and NULL. What does AVG(salary) return, and what might a stakeholder expect instead?
SUM over a column that is entirely NULL: does it return 0 or NULL? Why does that matter in a report?

sql-014.base: Does COUNT(DISTINCT) have a cost at scale?
variants: Counting distinct users per day over a year of clickstream is slow. What can you do?
When would an approximate distinct count be acceptable, and how much error does it typically add?

sql-015.base: How does your approach behave when a segment has an even number of orders?
variants: A segment has four orders: 10, 20, 40 and 100. What should the median be, and does your query return that?
Your query picks the middle row with ROW_NUMBER. What does it return for a segment with six orders?

sql-015.base: Why might you report the median rather than the mean here?
variants: A few enterprise orders are 100 times larger than the rest. Which summary do you show leadership, and why?
When would the mean be the more useful number for this segment?

sql-015.base: What does this cost on a billion-row table?
variants: Ranking every order in a billion-row table is too slow. What alternatives do you have?
Is an approximate percentile good enough for a weekly dashboard? How would you decide?
The two teams use different time windows to define a repeat purchase. What other differences would you look for?
Finance excludes refunded orders, and your dashboard includes them. List other choices that could explain a 7-point gap.

sql-016.base: How do you decide whose number is right?
variants: Both numbers are defensible. Who decides which one the company uses, and how?
The CFO asks which number is correct before a board meeting tomorrow. What do you say?

sql-016.base: How do you stop it happening again?
variants: What would you put in place so the next new metric doesn't diverge the same way?
How would a single metrics layer or documented definition help, and what does it cost to maintain?
